# AGENTS.md

Operating contract for every agent and automation working in this repository.
Read this first, then `docs/STATUS.md`, then `git log -10`.

## Documentation language

All repository artifacts are written in **English**: documentation, specs, ADRs, code comments, commit messages, status notes, and file names. Conversation with the owner may happen in any language; the repository does not. This applies to new files and to edits of existing ones.

## What this project is

Evengate is a personal software factory: a deterministic Rust control plane that moves work through an append-only event log and a fixed set of gates. The human is the owner and arbiter; agents execute and are checked by gates. v0 produces Rust projects only and is CLI-driven (binary `ev`, alias `evengate`).

## Non-negotiables

- **Event log is the source of truth.** All state is a pure `fold` over append-only events. `ev replay` must reconstruct byte-identical state.
- **Gates define completion.** The executing agent may never mark its own task done.
- **No async runtime.** No `tokio`, `reqwest`, `hyper`. Blocking threads and `std::sync` only.
- **Dependency budget.** At most 7 direct crates in `Cargo.toml`; each one justified.
- **Flat files, JSONL, git.** No database in v0.
- **Specs are Markdown with fixed headings** (`docs/spec.md` §8), not a DSL.
- **The name is the contract.** Any change that bypasses the event log or circumvents a gate is a regression by definition.

## Where things live

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `docs/spec.md` | Authoritative design. Change deliberately, bump the version line. |
| `docs/STATUS.md` | Session handoff. Rewritten every session; one screen. |
| `docs/DECISIONS.md` | Append-only decision log (ADR-lite). One entry per real decision. |
| `src/` | Code, laid out as `docs/spec.md` §7 specifies. |
| `tasks/` | Task specs produced and consumed by the factory. |

`docs/spec.md` is the single source of truth for design. Do not copy its content into `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, or `STATUS.md`; link instead.

## Work loop

1. Read `AGENTS.md`, `docs/STATUS.md`, `git log -10`.
2. Take the next item from `STATUS.md` → *Next*. If it is ambiguous, stop and ask the owner.
3. Implement the smallest vertical slice that satisfies the acceptance criteria.
4. Verify once, at the end, with the narrowest checks that cover the change:
   - `cargo check --locked`
   - `cargo test --locked`
   - `cargo clippy --locked -- -D warnings`
5. Rewrite `docs/STATUS.md` and append an ADR if a decision was made.
6. Commit with a one-line subject and a short body.
7. Push each logically completed slice to `origin` before starting the next one. Do not batch unrelated slices into a single push.
8. Before every push, scan the commit and any newly tracked files for sensitive data: API keys, tokens, private keys, passwords, `.env` or credential files, authenticated URLs, and absolute home paths that reveal the owner's machine. If anything is found, stop and ask the owner for explicit confirmation; never push it silently.

## Definition of done

- Behavior matches `docs/spec.md`; no stubs, placeholders, or "follow-up" deferrals.
- The checks in step 4 pass.
- `docs/STATUS.md` reflects the new reality.
- Decisions made along the way are in `docs/DECISIONS.md`.
- The slice is committed, scanned for sensitive data, and pushed.
- No unreferenced dead files, no duplicate specs, no chat transcripts committed.

## Writing `STATUS.md`

Rewrite, never append. Keep it under one screen:

```
Phase: ...
Done since last handoff: ...
In flight: ...
Next: ...
Blockers: ...
Open questions: ...
```

files.README.md:
# Evengate

A deterministic, Rust-native software factory that builds and improves itself under human oversight.

**Evengate** = *event* + *gate*: all state is derived from an append-only event log, and nothing moves without passing a gate.

Status: month 2 — self-edit tasks record a base tree, return partial edits, run Evengate's own gates on the copy, and open a PR whose diff contains only the change; the mandatory gates include `cargo fmt --check`, each task records its gate set, and merging across a gate-set change needs a reasoned human override. See `docs/STATUS.md`.

## Documentation

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`docs/spec.md`](docs/spec.md) | Authoritative design, v0.19 |
| [`docs/STATUS.md`](docs/STATUS.md) | Current phase, next step, blockers |
| [`docs/DECISIONS.md`](docs/DECISIONS.md) | Decision log with rationale |
| [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) | Rules for agents and contributors |

## Quickstart

```sh
docker build -f sandbox/Dockerfile -t evengate-sandbox:1.100 .   # once: clippy, rustfmt, locked deps
cargo build --locked

# start or resume a task; every task directory carries its own spec.md
cargo run --locked --bin ev -- run tasks/<task-dir>/spec.md

# verify recorded state and rebuild derived artifacts
cargo run --locked --bin ev -- replay tasks/sum-cli
cargo run --locked --bin ev -- materialize tasks/sum-cli

# after reviewing the branch:
cargo run --locked --bin ev -- approve <task-dir> --reviewer <your-name>

# when a gate blocks the task:
cargo run --locked --bin ev -- revise <task-dir> --reviewer <your-name> --reason "fix the failing test"
cargo run --locked --bin ev -- abandon <task-dir> --reviewer <your-name> --reason "not worth finishing"

# when a repeated lesson is proposed:
cargo run --locked --bin ev -- promote <task-dir> --reviewer <your-name>
cargo run --locked --bin ev -- dismiss <task-dir> --reviewer <your-name>
```

`tasks/hello` is the frozen seed-kernel run. It predates the mandatory review gate, so `ev replay tasks/hello` intentionally reports a pre-gate anomaly instead of matching its snapshot (ADR-0015).

Binaries: `ev` (daily use) and `evengate` (scripts, CI), both built from `src/main.rs`.

Environment: `EVENGATE_SANDBOX_IMAGE`, `EVENGATE_SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_SECS`, `EVENGATE_SANDBOX_MEMORY` (default `2g`), `EVENGATE_SANDBOX_CPUS` (default `2`), `EVENGATE_SANDBOX_PIDS` (default `256`), `EVENGATE_TEMPLATES`, `EVENGATE_LESSONS_DIR` (default `lessons/`), `EVENGATE_RULES_DIR` (default `rules/`).

Gate containers run read-only with no network, a read-only project mount, a 1 GiB executable `/tmp`, dropped capabilities, `no-new-privileges`, and the memory/PID/CPU caps above.

The executing agent defaults to the offline `TemplateClient`. Set `EVENGATE_LLM_URL` (an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint) to switch to `LiveClient`; `EVENGATE_LLM=template|live|recorded` overrides the choice. Live requests ask for a JSON object (`response_format`), so a model cannot return an unescaped-quote reply. Live mode reads `EVENGATE_LLM_API_KEY`, `EVENGATE_MODEL_EXECUTOR`/`_PLANNER`/`_REVIEWER` (fallback `EVENGATE_MODEL`), `EVENGATE_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECS`, and `EVENGATE_LLM_MAX_TOKENS`.

The `ReviewAgent` gate is mandatory and needs a model. With no endpoint configured, `ev run` executes the template agent and the four deterministic gates — `cargo check`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check` — then stops at the review gate with an actionable error; re-run with `EVENGATE_LLM_URL` set to finish the review and open the PR. `ev replay` is always offline.

A task spec with a `## Target` bullet under `src/` is a self-edit. `ev run` records the repository tree as `SelfEditBase` (without `.git`, `target`, `.tmp`, or generated task artifacts), seeds `tasks/<task-dir>/project/` from it, and sends only the target files plus a repository path map to the executor. The agent returns only changed files; they overlay the base. A single-file target returns that file as plain text (no JSON escaping), while a directory or multi-file target returns the manifest. The gates judge that copy in the sandbox, so the live checkout is untouched. A self-edit needs a model: the offline template agent refuses, because rendering `templates/bin` would replace Evengate with an unrelated crate. The review prompt sees only the files changed against the base, and the PR commits the base tree on `main` first, so the human reviews a diff. The sandbox image pre-fetches the locked dependency set at build time, so `cargo check`, `test`, `clippy`, and `fmt` run offline on the copy.

`TaskCreated` records the mandatory gate set in force for that task, so adding or removing a gate never reinterprets an old log. A task whose recorded set differs from the running binary's can merge only with `ev approve <task-dir> --reviewer <name> --reason <text>`; a bare approval stops at `RequestHumanReview`.

When a gate blocks a task, `ev revise` re-runs the executor with the failing verdicts, any human guidance, and the current project tree, then reruns every gate (at most two revisions). `ev abandon` ends a blocked task without a PR.

The review agent also returns 3–5 lessons. The executor writes them to `lessons/<task-id>.md`; both the next executor and the next reviewer prompt include the five most recent lesson files, and the reviewer is asked to copy a still-applicable lesson verbatim. The current spec always wins over inherited advice.

Project-wide rules live in `rules/<project>.md`, where `<project>` is the spec title slug. They join both the executor and the reviewer prompt on every invocation; a missing or blank file adds nothing, and an unreadable file fails the run.

After each review the executor groups similar lessons across `lessons/*.md` — stemmed content tokens with a Dice coefficient of at least 3/5, and no disagreement on negation. A group seen in three task files pauses the task before its PR: `ev promote` appends its representative wording to `rules/<project>.md` and continues; `ev dismiss` declines for that task. Dismissal is task-scoped, so a later task may propose the same unpromoted lesson again. Promotion stays a human decision; lexical matching can propose a near-miss, never apply one.

`project/` and `lessons/` are derived state. `ev materialize <task-dir>` rebuilds both from `events.jsonl` without a model or network: the last executor manifest becomes `project/`, and the last usable reviewer verdict becomes the lesson file. `state.json` is untouched. Only recorded files are recreated, so a local `.git` or `target/` inside `project/` is dropped; the bare remote under `artifacts/` is not.

## Working on it

Read `AGENTS.md`, then `docs/STATUS.md`. All repository documentation is written in English.
files.docs/DECISIONS.md:
# Decisions

Append-only. Newest at the bottom. One entry per real decision; do not edit past entries — supersede them with a new one.

Format:

```
## ADR-NNNN — Title
Date: YYYY-MM-DD
Status: accepted | superseded by ADR-NNNN
Decision: one sentence.
Why: the constraint that forced it.
Rejected: alternatives and why they lost.
```

---

## ADR-0001 — Repository documentation is English-only
Date: 2026-11-24
Status: accepted
Decision: All repository artifacts — docs, specs, ADRs, comments, commit messages, status notes — are written in English, regardless of the language used in conversation.
Why: Mixed-language documentation fragments search, diffing, and agent context; English is the common denominator for tooling and future contributors.
Rejected: Bilingual docs (duplication drifts); Russian-only (narrows tooling and audience).

## ADR-0002 — Documentation layout: spec, status, decisions, contract
Date: 2026-11-24
Status: accepted
Decision: Design truth lives in `docs/spec.md`; session handoff in `docs/STATUS.md`; rationale in `docs/DECISIONS.md`; agent/contributor rules in `AGENTS.md`; `README.md` is the human entry point only.
Why: One owner per kind of information prevents divergence. `STATUS.md` is rewritten each session; specs and ADRs change only deliberately.
Rejected: Single monolithic document (status churn pollutes design history); wiki/issue-tracker-only (outside the repo, not versioned with the code).

## ADR-0003 — Sandbox: Docker with a locally built Rust image
Date: 2026-11-24
Status: accepted
Decision: Gates run in Docker containers from `evengate-sandbox:1.100`, built once from `sandbox/Dockerfile`. Containers run with `--network=none`, a bind mount of a throwaway copy of the project, a 300 s timeout, and 1 MiB output caps.
Why: Docker is available on the target Windows machine, unlike `bwrap`. The official `rust:1.100` image ships without clippy and rustfmt, so those components are installed at image-build time and never at gate time; gates therefore stay offline and repeatable.
Rejected: `bwrap` (Linux-only); pulling the official image per gate (no clippy/rustfmt); installing components during a gate (needs network, breaks determinism).

## ADR-0004 — v0 pull requests are pushed branches in a local bare repository
Date: 2026-11-24
Status: accepted
Decision: `OpenPullRequest` commits the generated project on a branch named `ev/<project>` and pushes it to `tasks/<task>/artifacts/remote.git`; the `PrOpened` event records a `file://` URL with the branch. Git hosting (open question 3 in the spec) stays out of the kernel until week 3.
Why: The seed kernel must run offline and deterministically. A local bare remote exercises the real git CLI path — branch, commit, push — without credentials, network, or repository-creation APIs.
Rejected: GitHub API (adds network, tokens, and a repo-creation side effect to the kernel); `git request-pull` files (not a branch that can be reviewed or merged).

## ADR-0005 — Concurrency: task-level parallelism behind a coordination layer
Date: 2026-11-25
Status: accepted
Decision: v0 stays strictly sequential. Future parallelism runs N independent per-task state machines and adds only a coordination layer — a factory-level `factory.jsonl`, task claiming, a shared budget/rate limiter, and per-task git worktrees — leaving `Event`, `State`, `Command`, `reduce`, and `next_command` unchanged.
Why: Each task is already an independent event-sourced aggregate with its own log and replay, so the existing design parallelizes at the task boundary without touching schemas. A global sequence number would be a coordination point with no consumer; per-task order, wall-clock timestamps, and explicit `TaskDependsOn` events suffice. Building the scheduler before two `ev` processes run in two worktrees would automate an unproven design.
Rejected: Global event log or sequence number (serializes independent tasks, no consumer); reworking per-task logs (unnecessary); scheduling two workers on one task, cross-task dependencies, and distributed workers (each is a separate spec, out of scope for v0 and v1).

## ADR-0006 — Agent output is a JSON file manifest over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Date: 2026-11-27
Status: accepted
Decision: Every `LlmClient` returns a `{"files": {"relative/path": "contents"}}` manifest; the executor validates it, replaces `project/`, and only then runs gates. `LiveClient` speaks OpenAI-compatible chat completions configured entirely by environment variables; `TemplateClient` stays the deterministic offline default, and `RecordedClient` replays logged responses only when the role and prompt hash match.
Why: Gates judge files, not prose, so the agent boundary must produce a project tree in one recorded, bounded, diffable answer. A path→contents manifest is trivial to validate and record verbatim; the OpenAI-compatible wire format keeps spec §13.1 (provider and budget) a configuration decision, while `ureq` keeps the control plane blocking and free of an async runtime.
Rejected: Unified diffs (need a repository-state contract and fail opaquely); tool-call loops (scheduler-like complexity and more hidden state for no v0 consumer); hardcoding one vendor's API (forecloses §13.1); keeping the template copy outside the agent boundary (would leave response recording with no production consumer).

## ADR-0007 — ReviewAgent is a mandatory fourth gate that reviews the project tree
Date: 2026-11-27
Status: accepted
Decision: `ReviewAgent` is the last mandatory v0 gate. It runs after `Compiles`, `TestsPass`, and `LintsClean`, sends the task spec plus every project text file (excluding `.git` and `target`) to the Reviewer model, records the request and raw response as `AgentInvoked`/`AgentResponded` with role `reviewer`, and maps `{approve, issues[]}` to `Pass` or `Fail`. A withheld approval stops the run for a human immediately instead of re-asking the same tree; an unusable verdict becomes `NeedsHuman`. Without a model the gate refuses to run, and the task resumes at this gate once one is configured.
Why: The spec's gate table requires an LLM-backed review before the PR, and gates must judge the real artifact rather than the executing agent's summary. Re-sending a rejected artifact to the same model burns tokens without changing the artifact, so the human is the next step; recording the verdict and its token usage keeps replay deterministic and cost visible. A missing model must never become an implicit approval.
Rejected: A unified-diff input (needs a base tree that does not exist before the PR is opened, and adds a second artifact contract); automatic executor re-invocation on review failure (needs a revision phase and feedback-in-prompt plumbing; not in this slice); treating `TemplateClient` as a reviewer (self-certification by the executing agent); retrying the review gate (same artifact, extra cost, nondeterministic verdict).

## ADR-0008 — Gate failure recovery is a bounded, human-initiated revision
Date: 2026-11-27
Status: accepted
Decision: A task blocked by a gate (a verdict still failing after `MAX_GATE_ATTEMPTS`, or a review rejection) accepts `RevisionRequested` only in `Verifying`. The reducer snapshots the non-passing verdicts plus optional human guidance into `State`, clears all gate verdicts and attempt counters, increments a revision counter, and enters `Revising`; `next_command` re-invokes the executor once with those failures in its context, and the response returns the task to `Verifying` so every gate reruns on the new tree. Revisions are capped at `MAX_REVISIONS = 2`. `HumanAbandoned` ends any non-terminal task without a PR; `TaskAbandoned` stays the consequence of a human PR rejection.
Why: A blocked run with no path forward leaves the only recovery outside the event log (deleting state, editing files by hand). Revision keeps the loop inside the same contract: the executor is still the only producer of the artifact, the gates re-judge it, and the human decides when to spend another round. Snapshotting the verdicts in the reducer makes the re-invocation prompt a pure function of state and keeps replay byte-identical. Clearing attempts per revision is safe only because the revision count is bounded; together they cap total retries.
Rejected: Automatic re-invocation without a human event (the gate would become advisory and burn tokens indefinitely); carrying stale gate verdicts across revisions (the executor might replace the tree while the old passes still count); unbounded revisions (a broken template or endpoint could loop forever); a separate `RetryGate` command that resends the same tree (the review verdict is about the artifact, not the request); editing `project/` by hand between runs (unrecorded state outside the log).

## ADR-0009 — Committed task logs keep absolute home paths
Date: 2026-11-27
Status: accepted
Decision: `tasks/<task>/events.jsonl` and `state.json` may contain absolute paths from the owner's machine, such as `C:\Users\Dennis\...`, in recorded command output. These paths are not treated as sensitive and stay in the repository history. The pre-push scan still blocks API keys, tokens, private keys, passwords, credential files, and authenticated URLs.
Why: The event log is the evidence of a run and must replay byte-identically; rewriting recorded paths would either alter that evidence or require a history rewrite. A local username alone is low risk in the owner's personal repository, and the generated `project/` and `artifacts/` trees that produce most paths are already gitignored.
Rejected: Rewriting history and force-pushing (breaks every clone and commit SHA for a username); excluding logs from git (loses the replay evidence and `git log` trace); normalizing paths at write time (changes recorded command output and diverges from what the process actually printed).

## ADR-0010 — Lessons travel from the review verdict into the next executor prompt
Date: 2026-11-27
Status: accepted
Decision: The review protocol gains `lessons: [String]` (3–5 bullets). When the reviewer returns lessons, the executor writes `lessons/<task-id>.md` under the lessons root (`lessons/` in the working directory by default, `EVENGATE_LESSONS_DIR` overrides), overwriting the file on a revision. Executor prompt assembly reads the five most recent `*.md` files, newest first by modification time with file-name ties, and renders them under `# Lessons from previous tasks` with an explicit statement that the current spec and constraints win. No new event is added: the raw verdict stays in `AgentResponded`, which is the log source for the file. `rules/<project>.md` and `codebase-map.md` remain future slices.
Why: The reviewer is already the critic that judges the artifact, so asking it for lessons costs no extra call and keeps one agent boundary. Lessons must outlive `project/`, which is gitignored and replaced on every revision, so they live in a separate versioned directory. Recording the raw verdict preserves replay: `ev replay` stays a pure fold, while an execution replay can rebuild the file. Recency is the spec's designated order for v0; reading mtimes happens only in the impure executor, never in `reduce` or `next_command`.
Rejected: A separate planner call for lessons (extra tokens and a second protocol for the same critic); a `LessonRecorded` event (duplicates the verdict already in `AgentResponded` and has no state-machine consumer); writing lessons inside `project/` (destroyed by every revision and gitignored); a similarity index (spec defers it); ordering lessons by task id or a global counter (no global order exists without a coordination layer).

## ADR-0011 — Execution replay rebuilds project/ and lessons from the log
Date: 2026-11-27
Status: accepted
Decision: `ev materialize <task-dir>` applies `AgentResponded` events in log order to disk: each executor manifest replaces `project/`, and the last usable reviewer verdict rewrites `lessons/<task-id>.md`. It never calls a model, spawns a process, mutates `state.json`, or appends events.
Why: `project/` and the lesson file are gitignored derivatives of the log, so a fresh clone must be able to reproduce the artifact a human reviewed without spending tokens or trusting a hand-edited directory. Keeping it a separate command preserves the pure-fold contract of `ev replay`: replay proves state equality, materialize proves artifact equality. The executor already owns manifest validation and lesson writing, so reconstruction uses the same code path as the live run.
Rejected: Extending `ev replay` with side effects (makes the determinism check depend on disk state and weakens the name); rebuilding from `CommandExecuted` output (contains compiler noise, not the manifest); recording a separate materialized event (duplicates the log and has no reducer consumer); requiring the network or a model (defeats the purpose of deriving from the log).

## ADR-0012 — Gate containers are read-only and resource-capped
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted
Decision: Every gate container runs with `--init`, `--network=none`, `--read-only`, a read-only project bind mount, a 1 GiB executable `/tmp` tmpfs, `--memory`/`--memory-swap` 2 GiB, `--pids-limit` 256, `--cpus` 2, `--cap-drop=ALL`, and `no-new-privileges`. Memory, CPU, and PID caps are overridable with `EVENGATE_SANDBOX_MEMORY`, `EVENGATE_SANDBOX_CPUS`, and `EVENGATE_SANDBOX_PIDS`.
Why: Model-generated crates are untrusted code. The existing no-network, timeout, and output caps did not stop a build script or test from consuming host memory, forking without bound, spinning every core, or writing outside the disposable copy. A read-only root and project mount leave a bounded tmpfs as the only writable surface, and dropping capabilities removes privileged operations a root process in the container would otherwise retain. Docker 27 on the target Windows host accepts these flags, and a real `cargo test`/`cargo clippy` run passes with them.
Rejected: Leaving the rootfs writable (a build script can modify the image layer or `/etc`); a writable project mount (tests can mutate the artifact outside the log); swap instead of a hard memory cap (hides pressure and slows the host); per-gate bespoke limits (one policy, environment-overridable); `bwrap`/`firejail` (Linux-only, ADR-0003).

## ADR-0013 — Project rules are prompt context for the executor and the reviewer
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted
Decision: The executor and the review gate read `rules/<project>.md` at prompt-assembly time, where `<project>` is the spec-title slug and the root is `rules/` or `EVENGATE_RULES_DIR`. A present file becomes a `# Project rules` section after the task spec; a missing or blank file adds nothing; an unreadable file fails the invocation. Rules are never cached in `State`.
Why: Rules are human-authored project constraints, so a task must see them on first generation and on every revision, and the critic that approves the artifact must check the same constraints. Reading them inside the impure executor keeps `machine.rs` and `state.rs` pure, adds no event, and lets a human edit apply to the next invocation while the recorded prompt hash still proves which prompt produced the response. `codebase-map.md` stays out because v0 has no planner consumer.
Rejected: Storing rules in `State` (needs an event and a reducer rule for external, editable configuration); folding rules into `Spec` (breaks the immutable spec input and forces log rewrites when a rule changes); executor-only wiring (the reviewer could approve an artifact that violates a project rule); a `RuleRead` event (no reducer consumer and duplicates the file); silently ignoring an unreadable rules file (a gate-adjacent constraint must fail loudly).

## ADR-0014 — Lesson promotion pauses the task before its PR
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted
Decision: After a review writes lessons, the executor counts each canonical lesson once per lesson file across `lessons/*.md` and records `LessonRepeated` for counts of at least 3 that are not already bullets in `rules/<project>.md`. The reducer stores those counts. Once every gate passes, `machine.rs` emits `RequestHumanReview` with artifact kind `promotion` before `OpenPullRequest`. `ev promote` appends the lesson to `rules/<project>.md` and records `LessonPromoted`; `ev dismiss` records `LessonDismissed` only. One lesson is decided per invocation, in canonical key order; the task then asks for the next decision or continues.
Why: The spec requires a human decision on repeated lessons and the machine is pure, so repetition must reach `State` through events. Counting in the impure executor can see every task's lesson file; recording only the aggregate keeps `reduce` free of I/O and replay a pure fold. Pausing after the gates means the artifact already exists and no tokens are spent after the proposal. `RequestHumanReview` already means "stop for a human", so reusing it keeps one interaction path. Dismissal is task-scoped because per-task logs have no factory projection (ADR-0005); the next task proposes an unpromoted lesson again.
Rejected: Counting inside `reduce` (reads files, breaks purity and byte-identical replay); a global promotion log (coordination layer out of scope, ADR-0005); writing `rules/` automatically (promotion is a human decision); a separate `Promote` command variant (duplicates the review stop and its CLI path); appending dismissed lessons to rules (would make them binding prompt content); blocking before the review gate (the decision could change the rules after a review call was already paid for).

## ADR-0015 — The seed-kernel hello log is frozen historical evidence
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted
Decision: `tasks/hello` stays in the repository unchanged as the record of the week-1–2 seed run. Its committed `state.json` is not regenerated, and `ev replay tasks/hello` reports the `merged without passed gates and human approval` anomaly because the log predates the mandatory `ReviewAgent` gate (ADR-0007). The byte-identical replay guarantee is scoped to the reducer that produced the snapshot; a later gate-set change surfaces as an anomaly, never as a rewritten snapshot.
Why: The log is the first end-to-end proof of the name — template, sandbox gates, PR, human merge — and deleting or overwriting it destroys the only record of that milestone. Regenerating it needs a live reviewer, spends tokens, and contradicts the task's own spec ("No review agent") while replacing the historical snapshot with a different run. Appending a synthetic `ReviewAgent` pass would be gate circumvention by definition. Replaying the log remains a pure fold; the mismatch is the honest signal that the mandatory gate set grew.
Rejected: Regenerating the snapshot with a live model (cost, credentials, and it replaces evidence with a new artifact); appending a `review_agent` pass event (fabricated completion, violates "gates define completion"); deleting the task (loses the seed-run record); grandfathering tasks by creation time (weakens the mandatory gate set for every future replay).

## ADR-0016 — Lesson repetition is lexical similarity, not exact text
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted
Decision: `count_lessons` groups bullets by the Dice coefficient of their stemmed content-token sets (threshold 3/5), after lowercasing, dropping stopwords and generic advice framing, and folding simple English plurals. A negation (`not`, `no`, `never`, `avoid`, `cannot`) on one side and not the other blocks a match. A group counts once per task file; its representative is the exact spelling found in the most files, ties broken by canonical key. Rule deduplication, the "already promoted" check, and `--lesson` selection use the same matcher. This supersedes the exact-text sentence in ADR-0014.
Why: exact canonical matching required three independent reviews to emit a byte-identical sentence, which made the promotion pause practically unreachable — the reviewer sees the spec and artifact, not prior lessons, so it has no reason to repeat wording. Paraphrases are the normal case. Lexical grouping makes the designed feedback loop observable without a model, a vector index, or a new crate, and promotion stays a human decision, so a false merge is reviewed rather than applied.
Rejected: exact matching (never fires in practice); lowering `PROMOTION_THRESHOLD` to 2 (changes how much evidence a rule needs and still misses paraphrases); embeddings or an external NLP crate (network, dependency budget, non-determinism, and the vector store the spec defers); a full stemming algorithm (more surface for false merges than the conservative plural fold needs); transitive single-linkage clustering (a chain of weak overlaps can merge unrelated advice, so each group is anchored to its most-supported spelling).

## ADR-0017 — The review agent sees recent lessons and reuses their wording
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted
Decision: The review prompt carries the five most recent `lessons/*.md` files — the same section the executor sees — and instructs the reviewer to copy an earlier lesson's text exactly when it still applies. New issues still get new wording.
Why: Promotion counts a lesson across tasks, but the reviewer's information set did not include prior lessons, so it reworded every observation. Three real runs produced three lesson files with a maximum cross-file Dice of 0.44, so the promotion pause never fired. Repetition is only meaningful if the critic knows what has already been said; verbatim reuse also keeps the promoted rule stable instead of choosing one paraphrase arbitrarily. The reviewer still judges the current artifact, not the earlier verdicts, and the current spec and rules win.
Rejected: Relying on lexical similarity alone (real paraphrases are too divergent — measured); a lower threshold (it would approach 0.2 and merge distinct advice); semantic embeddings (dependency, network, non-determinism, and the deferred vector store); letting the executor copy lessons (the critic, not the executor, owns the lesson verdict); a per-prior-lesson "still applies" boolean in the response schema (changes the contract and needs a merge rule for the promoted text).

## ADR-0018 — LiveClient requests JSON object responses
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted
Decision: Every `LiveClient` request sets `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}`. Both roles already promise one JSON object; the server now enforces it.
Why: Local OpenAI-compatible servers emitted JSON with unescaped quotes inside Rust source (`println!("{}", sum)`), so the manifest could not parse and no event was recorded. JSON mode constrains decoding at the server and fixed it without post-processing model text. The field is standard in the OpenAI-compatible wire format; providers that ignore it behave as before.
Rejected: Repairing invalid JSON client-side (cannot distinguish a structural quote from a content quote); retrying until the model escapes correctly (nondeterministic and wasteful); base64 or a line envelope for file contents (larger protocol change for the same result); making JSON mode optional (both roles require JSON, so there is no case for off).

## ADR-0019 — FormatClean is the fourth deterministic gate
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted
Decision: `GateId::FormatClean` runs `cargo fmt --check` in the sandbox, after `LintsClean` and before `ReviewAgent`. The mandatory v0 set grows to five gates. The repository tree is rustfmt-clean under the pinned 1.100 toolchain, and `gate.rs` tests assert the command, slug, label, diff-line failure detail, and that the mandatory set only grows.
Why: Formatting is deterministic, offline, and cheap, and `cargo fmt --check` prints the first offending location, which is useful revision feedback. The sandbox image already installs rustfmt at build time (ADR-0003), so the gate needs no image, network, or dependency change. This is the first Month 2 self-edit.
Rejected: Running `cargo fmt` without `--check` (a gate must judge, never mutate the artifact); folding formatting into clippy (clippy does not check rustfmt output); formatting inside the executor (the executing agent would be marking its own work); a separate formatting service or tool (new dependency for a command already in the image).

## ADR-0020 — Gate sets are recorded per task, and drift needs a reasoned override
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted
Decision: `TaskCreated` records the mandatory gate set in force (`gates`). `State.gates` carries that set for the task and `machine.rs` iterates it; logs written before the field fold to `LEGACY_V0` (the pre-`FormatClean` four) and serialize without the field, so replay stays byte-identical. Every phase change resets `State.phase_invocations`, and `next_command` stops with `RequestHumanReview` after `MAX_AGENT_INVOCATIONS_PER_PHASE = 5`. A task whose recorded set differs from the running binary's `MANDATORY_V0` cannot reach `Finalize { Merged }` on a bare approval: `ev approve --reason <text>` records `HumanApproved { reviewer, reason }`, the only override. A test asserts `LEGACY_V0` remains a subset of `MANDATORY_V0`.
Why: Adding `FormatClean` to a global list would have made every previously merged log fail `all_mandatory_passed`, turn its `Merged` event into an anomaly, and break the byte-identical replay guarantee. Recording the set in the event is the event-sourced answer: a task is judged by the gates it was created under, and gate-set history becomes explicit instead of implicit in the binary. The subset test is what rejects a self-edit that removes a historical gate: the artifact's own `TestsPass` gate fails. The reasoned approval is the merge-time guard for any drift the test cannot see, with no silent reconciliation. The per-phase counter is derived by the reducer, reset on every transition, and omitted when zero, so committed terminal snapshots and old logs stay unchanged.
Rejected: Reinterpreting old logs under the current set (breaks replay and rewrites evidence); recording a separate `GateSetVersion` event (duplicates `TaskCreated` and adds a second reducer input); making every approval carry a reason (noise, since only a real set difference needs one); keeping the counter in the executor (would break the pure `next_command` contract); diffing the artifact in `machine.rs` to detect gate edits (the machine has no base tree and the executor cannot certify its own artifact); relying on review alone (a gate weakening would be invisible to the machine and to replay).

## ADR-0021 — Self-edit tasks are marked by `## Target` and start from a repository copy
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted
Decision: `Spec` gains an optional `target` list parsed from a `## Target` section. A target equal to `src` or starting with `src/` makes the task a self-edit. On its first invocation the executor finds the nearest ancestor of the task directory that contains `.git`, `Cargo.toml`, and `src/`, copies that repository into `project/` (skipping `.git`, `target`, `.tmp`, and generated `tasks/*/project` and `tasks/*/artifacts`), and sends the copied tree to the model. The prompt requires the complete tree back because the manifest replaces `project/`; the offline `TemplateClient` refuses the task. Targets must exist in the copy. Empty targets serialize like a legacy spec, so old logs replay byte-identically.
Why: The self-edit workflow needs a base artifact, and the event log must record how the task was classified. Deriving the base from the task directory rather than the caller's working directory keeps the copy deterministic and independent of where `ev` is invoked. A spec field is recorded inside `TaskCreated`, unlike an environment variable or CLI flag, so replay reaches the same conclusion. The copy is the separate checkout the gates judge: `project/` is gitignored and disposable, and the live tree is never mutated. Refusing `TemplateClient` prevents a self-edit from silently replacing the repository with `templates/bin`.
Rejected: An `EVENGATE_SELF_EDIT` environment variable or `--self-edit` flag (unrecorded, so replay could not reconstruct the decision); inferring a self-edit from the project slug (magic and easy to rename); copying from the process working directory (breaks when `ev` runs from another directory); keeping the live tree as `project/` (gates would mutate the repository); overlay manifests with deletions (needs a base-tree contract in the log; a full-tree manifest keeps `materialize` self-contained); refusing without a model but still seeding (leaves a misleading checkout after a failed run).

## ADR-0022 — The sandbox image pre-fetches Evengate's locked dependencies
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted
Decision: `sandbox/Dockerfile` is built with the repository root as context, installs clippy and rustfmt, then runs `cargo fetch --locked` in `/opt/evengate-deps` against `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`. `.dockerignore` excludes `.git`, `.tmp`, `target`, and generated task trees. Gate containers remain `--network=none` with `CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true`. `validate_path` also rejects `:` so a Windows drive prefix is rejected identically on Linux.
Why: A self-edit gate compiles Evengate, whose sources depend on `serde`, `serde_json`, and `ureq`; the previous image had an empty registry and failed with `no matching package named serde found`, so the self-edit path could not reach a gate. Fetching at image-build time is the only place network is available while gates stay offline and repeatable. The cross-platform colon check surfaced because the same tests now run in Linux. Updating the build context is required for the image to see the manifests.
Rejected: Running self-edit gates on the host (breaks the sandbox invariant and pushes network into the gate); mounting the host cargo registry (environment-specific and non-reproducible); vendoring crates into `project/` (huge manifests, binary-ish files in the PR, and review noise); allowing network during gates (nondeterministic); accepting the failing test on Linux (the artifact's own `TestsPass` gate would block every self-edit).

## ADR-0023 — Self-edits record a base tree and return partial manifests
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted; supersedes the full-tree requirement in ADR-0021
Decision: `ev run` records the repository tree as `SelfEditBase` immediately after `TaskCreated`, before any model call, excluding `.git`, `target`, `.tmp`, and generated task trees. The executor prompt carries only the `## Target` files plus a repository path map; the model returns only the changed files. A self-edit manifest overlays `project/` instead of replacing it, and deletions are unsupported in v0. `ev materialize` writes `SelfEditBase` first and then overlays every executor manifest. The review prompt carries the repository path map and only the files that differ from the base. The offline `TemplateClient` still refuses self-edits.
Why: The full-tree protocol was unusable with the available local model. The repository prompt was about 414 KB (roughly 103k tokens) while `qwen2.5-coder:14b` has a 32k context, and the required full-tree response exceeds any practical output budget even on a 131k-context model. Recording the base in the log keeps materialization independent of the live checkout, while a target-scoped prompt and partial response fit the model and keep the log small. Overlay semantics match "edit these files"; rejecting deletions is an explicit v0 limit rather than a silent data-loss path.
Rejected: Keeping the full-tree protocol and using a hosted model (not available in the runtime and still expensive for a 400 KB echo); scoping only the prompt while replacing the tree (would delete every unlisted file); ambient base reconstruction from the live repository (not replayable after the repository moves); deleting files through the manifest (needs a second response field and a deletion policy; deferred); silent partial replacement (a stale artifact without a recorded base).

## ADR-0024 — A self-edit PR commits the base tree before the change
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted
Decision: When a self-edit opens its PR and `project/` has no Git history yet, the executor moves the edited tree aside, writes the recorded `SelfEditBase` files into `project/`, initializes Git, and commits that tree on `main` as `ev: initialize <project>`. It then clears the worktree (keeping `.git`), restores the edited tree, checks out `ev/<project>`, and commits the change. Generated projects keep the existing empty base commit. `git diff main..ev/<project>` therefore contains only the self-edit.
Why: An empty base made every self-edit PR a repository-sized addition, so the human could not review the change. The base tree is already in the event log (ADR-0023), so the base commit is reproducible from the log and needs no live checkout. Reusing the existing push path keeps one PR implementation.
Rejected: Keeping the empty base (unreviewable diff); creating the base commit from the live repository (drifts from the recorded base and breaks replay); pushing only a patch file (not a branch that can be reviewed or merged); a separate `git worktree` per task (more moving parts for one commit).

## ADR-0025 — A single-file self-edit returns plain text, not JSON
Date: 2026-11-28
Status: accepted
Decision: When a self-edit has exactly one `## Target` that names an existing file, the request switches to `RequestFormat::SingleFile`: the system prompt becomes a strict code-editor instruction, the prompt hash includes the format, the user prompt asks for that file's complete contents and nothing else, and the request omits `response_format`, because a JSON-mode constraint forced the model to answer `{}`. The response is treated as the file, with an optional Markdown fence unwrapped and a trailing newline ensured. A directory target or several targets keeps the JSON manifest and the default system prompt. `ev materialize` applies the same rule from the recorded base.
Why: The first real self-edit with `qwen2.5-coder:14b` returned a truncated JSON manifest. The value ended at the first unescaped quote in `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`; the parser accepted the resulting valid-but-short string and the artifact failed at `cargo check` with an unclosed delimiter. JSON escaping of Rust attributes is the fragile part, and Ollama ignored `response_format`. Plain text has no escaping layer and fits the single-file case. The deterministic gates still judge the result.
Rejected: Relying on JSON mode (the local server ignored it); a stronger escaping instruction (probabilistic, and the model failed at the first quote); a custom diff protocol (still needs quoting or a parser); always using raw text (ambiguous for multiple files); accepting the truncated artifact (the artifact's own gates rejected it).

# Status

Last updated: 2026-11-28

**Phase:** Month 2 continues. The self-edit path is now usable with a local model: the repository base is recorded in the log, the executor sees only target files, responses overlay that base, the reviewer sees only the changed files, and the PR diff contains only the change.

**Done since last handoff:**
- `TaskCreated` is followed by `SelfEditBase`, the repository tree recorded before any model call (excluding `.git`, `target`, `.tmp`, and generated task trees). The task log is sufficient to rebuild `project/` and the PR base.
- A self-edit executor prompt carries the `## Target` files and a repository path map, not the whole tree. The response manifest overlays `project/`; unlisted files survive. Deletions are not supported in v0. The offline `TemplateClient` still refuses self-edits.
- The review prompt for a self-edit carries the task spec, the path map, and only the files that differ from `SelfEditBase`, plus a deleted-file list. A non-self-edit task still reviews the complete project.
- `ev materialize` writes `SelfEditBase` first and then overlays every executor response, so execution replay needs no live checkout.
- A self-edit PR commits `SelfEditBase` on `main` as `ev: initialize <project>` before the feature branch; `git diff main..ev/<project>` contains only the change. Generated projects keep the empty base commit.
- The first two real self-edit attempts exposed model failures: `qwen2.5-coder:14b` truncated the JSON manifest at the first unescaped serde attribute quote, and `llama3.1:8b` returned a JSON map instead of the file. A single-file self-edit now switches to `RequestFormat::SingleFile`, whose system prompt demands the file and nothing else; the format is in the prompt hash, the request omits JSON mode, a fence is unwrapped, and a trailing newline is ensured. A third attempt returned `{}` because JSON mode was still set; that task was also abandoned and removed.
- Checks: 108 tests per binary, `cargo check --locked`, `cargo clippy --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check` pass. `sum-cli` (37), `sum-cli-nary` (39), `sum-cli-help` (47), and `word-count` (28) replay byte-identically.

**In flight:** nothing.

**Next:**
1. Run the first real self-edit through the factory: write `tasks/<task-id>/spec.md` with a small, testable change and a `## Target` under `src/`, point `EVENGATE_LLM_URL` at the local Ollama endpoint, run `ev run`, review the PR diff, and merge the reviewed change.
2. After that run, decide whether a self-edit task should be able to delete a file; the current overlay protocol has no deletion field.

**Blockers:** none.

# Evengate — Technical Specification v0.19

> A deterministic, Rust-native software factory that builds and improves itself under human oversight, and later produces pet projects in a familiar way.

**Changes from v0.18:** a self-edit with exactly one file target returns that file's complete contents as plain text, not a JSON manifest, so a Rust attribute quote cannot truncate the response. Multiple targets or a directory target keep the manifest (§7.4, §7.5, ADR-0025).

**Changes from v0.17:** self-edits are partial. `TaskCreated` is followed by `SelfEditBase`, a recorded repository tree; the executor sees only the target files plus a repository path map and returns only changed files; the review gate sees only files changed against the base; and the PR commits the base tree on `main` before the feature branch, so the human reviews a diff (§7.1, §7.4–§7.6, §10.2, ADR-0023, ADR-0024).

**Changes from v0.16:** a spec can name `## Target` files; when one targets `src/`, the executor bases `project/` on a copy of this repository, refuses the offline template agent, and requires the complete tree. The sandbox image pre-fetches the locked dependency set so Evengate's own gates build offline (§7.4, §7.7, §8, §10.2, ADR-0021, ADR-0022).

**Changes from v0.15:** the mandatory set gains `FormatClean` (`cargo fmt --check`); every task records the gate set in force at creation, so a later gate change never reinterprets an old log, and merging under a different set requires an explicit `HumanApproved { reason }`; agent invocations are budgeted per phase (§7.1–§7.3, §7.6, §10.2, §10.3, ADR-0019, ADR-0020).

**Changes from v0.14:** the review prompt now carries the five most recent lesson files and instructs verbatim reuse of a still-applicable lesson, so repetition is observable for promotion; `LiveClient` requests `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` so a local model cannot return an unescaped-quote reply (§7.5, §7.8, ADR-0017, ADR-0018).

**Changes from v0.13:** promotion treats paraphrased lessons as repetitions — stemmed content-token sets with a Dice threshold of 3/5 and a negation guard — instead of requiring identical text (§7.8, ADR-0016).

**Changes from v0.12:** the replay guarantee is scoped to the reducer that produced the snapshot; `tasks/hello` is frozen as seed-run evidence and is expected to replay with the pre-`ReviewAgent` anomaly (§6.3, §14, ADR-0015).

**Changes from v0.11:** a lesson seen in three tasks now pauses the task before its PR; `ev promote` adds it to `rules/`, `ev dismiss` declines for that task (§7.8, ADR-0014).

**Changes from v0.10:** project-wide `rules/<project>.md` now joins every executor and reviewer prompt, read from the rules root (`rules/` by default, `EVENGATE_RULES_DIR` overrides) at prompt-assembly time (§7.8, ADR-0013).

**Changes from v0.9:** gate containers gain read-only filesystems, read-only project mounts, a bounded writable `/tmp`, and memory, swap, PID, and CPU caps; capabilities are dropped and privileges cannot escalate (§7.7, ADR-0012).

**Changes from v0.8:** `ev materialize <task-id>` is execution replay: it rebuilds the gitignored `project/` tree and `lessons/<task-id>.md` from `AgentResponded` events in log order, without a model or network (§6.3, §7.4, §7.8, ADR-0011).

**Changes from v0.7:** a revision prompt now carries the project tree the gates judged instead of the reference template, and a gate failure reports the first actionable diagnostic rather than cargo's `Compiling`/`Checking` status line (§7.3, §7.4).

**Changes from v0.6:** the review agent returns 3–5 lessons; the executor writes them to `lessons/<task-id>.md`, and the next executor prompt carries the five most recent lesson files (§7.5, §7.6, §7.8, ADR-0010).

**Changes from v0.5:** gate-blocked tasks have a bounded revision path — `ev revise` re-invokes the executor with the failing gate verdicts and optional human guidance, and `ev abandon` ends a blocked task without opening a PR (§7.2, §7.3, §7.6, ADR-0008).

**Changes from v0.4:** the `ReviewAgent` gate is mandatory and LLM-backed; it reviews the project tree after the deterministic gates and stops for a human when approval is withheld (§7.6, ADR-0007).

**Changes from v0.3:** the model boundary is concrete — a JSON file-manifest agent protocol, an OpenAI-compatible `LiveClient` over `ureq`, a prompt-hash-checked `RecordedClient`, and the offline `TemplateClient` as the default (§7.5, ADR-0006).

**Changes from v0.2:** concurrency settled as post-v1 task-level parallelism (§13.6, ADR-0005); no event-log rework required.

**Changes from v0.1:** the project is now named **Evengate** (event + gate). CLI is `ev` (short) / `evengate` (explicit). Crate and repository are `evengate`. A dedicated Naming section was added. The "event sourcing over reactive streams" principle was made explicit. All `factory`-prefixed identifiers were renamed.

## 1. Overview

**Evengate** is a personal software factory: a deterministic control plane written in Rust that orchestrates LLM agents through a strict, gate-checked pipeline. The human is the **owner and arbiter**; Evengate is the **executor and critic**. Over time Evengate grows its own capabilities, accumulates structured knowledge from every task, and reduces the human's role from coder to reviewer to occasional arbiter.

Evengate is **self-hosting in the goal, not in the starting point**: it cannot bootstrap itself from nothing. A minimal human-written **seed kernel** is required. After that, Evengate extends itself under human review.

|---|------|---------------------|
| G1 | Deterministic control plane | Same event log → byte-identical state, regardless of when replayed |

## 4. Non-Goals (v0)

- **Not** a general problem-solver for non-software domains.
- **Not** fully autonomous. Human review is required for every merge in v0.
- **Not** multi-stack. v0 produces **Rust projects only**.
- **Not** a web service. CLI + filesystem is the interface in v0.
- **Not** async. Blocking threads only.
- **Not** a database-backed system. Flat files + JSONL, versioned in git.
- **Not** a DSL for specs. Markdown with fixed headings.

## 5. Design Principles

1. **Determinism at the control layer.** State machine and event reduction are pure Rust functions. LLM calls, process execution, and filesystem I/O live behind explicit boundaries.
2. **Event sourcing as the foundation.** All state derives from an append-only event log. Replay is a first-class operation.
3. **Isolation of the non-deterministic.** The LLM lives behind an `LlmClient` trait. Recording and replaying LLM responses is how determinism survives across runs.
4. **Gates define completion.** Executors produce artifacts; gates decide whether artifacts are acceptable.
5. **Minimal dependencies.** Every crate must justify itself against a hand-rolled alternative.
6. **Blocking over async.** Threads and `std::sync` channels. No `tokio`, no `reqwest`, no `hyper`.
7. **Markdown specs, not DSLs.** Human-readable, diff-able, parseable with ~30 lines of Rust.
8. **Flat files over databases.** Git-versioned state is debuggable, replayable, and diffable. Databases come only when profiling proves they are needed.
9. **Cost visibility from day one.** Token usage and money are logged per event.
10. **No self-certification.** The executing agent cannot mark a task complete.
11. **Event sourcing over reactive streams.** The event log is the single source of truth; all derived state is a `fold` over it. Reactive libraries (`Rx`, `futures::Stream`) are deliberately excluded from the control plane because they introduce schedulers and async composition, both of which break byte-identical replay. Reactive ideas are borrowed as *patterns* (multiple projections, backpressure as budget gates), not as dependencies.
12. **The name is the contract.** *Event* and *gate* are not branding — they are the two invariants that must never be weakened. Any change that bypasses the event log or circumvents a gate is a regression by definition.

## 6. Architecture

### 6.1 High-level layers

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  CLI (main.rs) — `ev` / `evengate`                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  machine.rs   ← pure: fn next_command(state) -> Cmd │
│  state.rs     ← pure: fn reduce(state, event) -> St │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  executor.rs  ← side effects: executes Command,     │
│                  appends Event                      │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  llm/         ← trait LlmClient (recorded | live)   │
│  gate.rs      ← deterministic checks + review agent │
│  sandbox.rs   ← process isolation via external bin  │
│  knowledge.rs ← read/write structured artifacts     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 6.2 The determinism boundary

| Layer | Deterministic? | How |
|-------|----------------|-----|
| `machine.rs` | Yes | Pure function, no I/O, no time, no randomness |
| `state.rs` | Yes | Pure `reduce` over immutable events |
| `event.rs` | Yes | Serialization is stable (JSONL with sorted keys) |
| `executor.rs` | No (by design) | Wraps side effects; emits events |
| `llm/` | No (by design) | Live impl calls the API; `recorded` impl replays from the log |
| `gate.rs` | Partially | Most gates deterministic; review gate is LLM-backed and recorded |
| `sandbox.rs` | No (by design) | Spawns processes |

**Rule:** if code in `machine.rs` or `state.rs` needs I/O, time, or randomness, it must be refactored into a `Command` emitted from `machine.rs` and executed by `executor.rs`.

### 6.3 Event sourcing model

Every task lives in its own directory:

```
tasks/<task-id>/
  spec.md         -- immutable input (markdown spec)
  events.jsonl    -- append-only event log
  state.json      -- denormalized snapshot (derived, regenerable)
  artifacts/      -- produced files, patches, logs
```

**Replay guarantee:** `ev replay <task-id>` reads `events.jsonl`, folds through `reduce`, and produces a `State` identical to the live run when the snapshot was written by the same reducer. Live LLM responses are recorded as events, so replay never calls the network. The guarantee is about determinism, not backward compatibility: when the reducer changes, replaying an older log records the resulting anomaly and reports the snapshot mismatch instead of rewriting history. A gate-set change no longer reinterprets old tasks, because each `TaskCreated` records the gates in force at the time; logs that predate that field fold to `LEGACY_V0`. `tasks/hello` remains the pre-snapshot exception (§14, ADR-0015).

**Execution replay:** `ev materialize <task-id>` reconstructs the gitignored `project/` tree and `lessons/<task-id>.md` from `AgentResponded` events in log order. A generated project keeps the last executor manifest; a self-edit first writes its recorded `SelfEditBase` and then overlays every executor manifest, so the same log recreates the same tree without the live checkout. The last usable reviewer verdict supplies the lesson. It calls no model, spawns nothing, and leaves `state.json` untouched, so the pure-fold guarantee of `ev replay` is unchanged. Only recorded files are recreated: a local `.git` or `target/` inside `project/` is dropped, and the bare remote under `artifacts/` is untouched.

**Formal contract:**

```rust
fn reduce(state: State, event: Event) -> State   // pure, total
fn next_command(state: &State) -> Option<Command> // pure, deterministic
```

`next_command` returns `None` only when the task is in a terminal state (merged, rejected, or abandoned).

### 6.4 Command / Event cycle

```rust
loop {
    match machine::next_command(&state) {
        None => break,
        Some(cmd) => {
            let events = executor::run(cmd, &ctx)?;  // side effects happen here
            for ev in events {
                log::append(&ev)?;
                state = state::reduce(state, ev);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

The loop is boring on purpose. All intelligence lives in `next_command` and in the gates.

## 7. Module Breakdown

### 7.1 `event.rs` — the event vocabulary

```rust
pub enum Event {
    TaskCreated { spec: Spec, gates: Vec<GateId> },
    SelfEditBase { files: BTreeMap<String, String> },
    AgentInvoked { role: AgentRole, prompt_hash: String },
    AgentResponded { role: AgentRole, response: String, tokens: TokenUsage },
    CommandExecuted { cmd: String, exit_code: i32, stdout: String, stderr: String },
    GateEvaluated { gate: GateId, result: GateResult },
    HumanApproved { reviewer: String, reason: Option<String> },
    HumanRejected { reviewer: String, reason: String },
    RevisionRequested { reviewer: String, guidance: Option<String> },
    HumanAbandoned { reviewer: String, reason: String },
    LessonRepeated { lesson: String, text: String, count: u32 },
    LessonPromoted { reviewer: String, lesson: String },
    LessonDismissed { reviewer: String, lesson: String },
    PrOpened { url: String },
    Merged { commit: String },
    TaskAbandoned { reason: String },
    Tick { now_unix: u64 },
}
```

All events are serialized as JSON Lines with stable field ordering. The log is the single source of truth.

### 7.2 `state.rs` — the reducer

```rust
pub struct State {
    pub phase: Phase,           // Drafting, Generating, Verifying, Revising, Reviewing, Merged, ...
    pub spec: Spec,
    pub gates: Vec<GateId>,     // recorded at TaskCreated; never re-derived
    pub artifacts: Vec<ArtifactRef>,
    pub gate_results: HashMap<GateId, GateResult>,
    pub phase_invocations: u32, // loop-protection budget for the current phase
    pub token_spend: TokenUsage,
    pub human_decision: Option<HumanDecision>,
}
```

`reduce` must be total: every `(State, Event)` pair produces a valid `State`, even if the event is unexpected in the current phase (in which case it is recorded as an anomaly, not a panic). The gate set is part of the task, not of the reducer: logs written before it was recorded fold to `LEGACY_V0`.

### 7.3 `machine.rs` — the deterministic policy

```rust
pub fn next_command(state: &State) -> Option<Command> { ... }

pub enum Command {
    InvokeAgent { role: AgentRole, context: Context },
    RunGate { gate: GateId },
    RequestHumanReview { artifact: ArtifactRef },
    OpenPullRequest { branch: String },
    AwaitHuman,
    Finalize { outcome: Outcome },
}
```

**Invariants enforced here:**

- `InvokeAgent` is never issued for a role that already produced a response in the current phase without an intervening gate.
- `Finalize { Merged }` is unreachable unless every gate in the task's recorded set passed **and** a `HumanApproved` event exists.
- A task whose recorded gate set differs from the running binary's `MANDATORY_V0` can merge only through `HumanApproved { reason }`; a bare approval leaves it at `RequestHumanReview`.
- No command is issued twice in a row with identical parameters (loop protection): each branch is keyed by a verdict or counter that only an intervening event changes, `MAX_AGENT_INVOCATIONS_PER_PHASE = 5` stops a phase that stops advancing, gate retries are capped at `MAX_GATE_ATTEMPTS = 2`, and revisions at `MAX_REVISIONS = 2`.

**Revision path.** A gate that still fails after `MAX_GATE_ATTEMPTS`, or a review rejection, leaves the task in `Verifying` with `RequestHumanReview`. The human may then issue `RevisionRequested`, which is accepted only in `Verifying` with at least one non-passing verdict. The reducer snapshots those verdicts and the optional guidance into `State`, increments the revision counter, clears every gate verdict and attempt counter, and enters `Revising`. `next_command` then issues one `InvokeAgent` whose `Context` carries the failures and whose prompt includes the current project tree; the response moves the task to `Generating` and back to `Verifying`, so every gate runs again on the new tree. Revisions are capped at `MAX_REVISIONS` (2); at the cap the machine requests a human again. `HumanAbandoned` ends the task from any non-terminal phase, while `TaskAbandoned` remains the consequence of rejecting a PR.

### 7.4 `executor.rs` — the impure boundary

Thin. For each `Command`, the executor:

1. Performs the side effect (LLM call, process spawn, git operation).
2. Emits one or more `Event`s.
3. Returns them for the outer loop to log and reduce.

The executor must never mutate `State` directly. It only returns events. A failing deterministic gate records one reason line: the first compiler error code, test panic, clippy warning, or generic error, in that order; cargo's progress lines are skipped because they are useless to a revision prompt.

The same module owns `materialize`: it applies recorded executor manifests and reviewer lessons to disk in log order. It is the impure counterpart to `ev replay`, not part of the `Command` loop, and it never changes the log or the snapshot.

**Self-edit tasks.** A spec whose `## Target` lists a path under `src/` is a self-improvement task (§10.2). When `ev run` creates the task, it reads this repository — excluding `.git`, `target`, `.tmp`, and the generated `tasks/*/project` and `tasks/*/artifacts` trees — and records it as `SelfEditBase` immediately after `TaskCreated`. The base is therefore in the log before any model call, and `project/` is rebuilt from it rather than from the live checkout. The executor prompt carries the target files and a repository path map; the agent returns only the files it changed. A single-file self-edit returns that file as plain text; a directory or multi-file self-edit returns the manifest. The response overlays `project/`, so an unlisted file survives; deletions are not supported in v0. The copy is the separate checkout the deterministic gates judge in the sandbox, so the live working tree is never mutated. The offline `TemplateClient` refuses a self-edit, because rendering `templates/bin` would replace Evengate with an unrelated crate. When the PR opens, `main` is committed from `SelfEditBase` first, so the feature branch is a real diff.

### 7.5 `llm/` — the model boundary

```rust
pub trait LlmClient {
    fn complete(&self, req: &LlmRequest) -> Result<LlmResponse, String>;
}

pub struct LlmRequest { pub role: AgentRole, pub prompt: String }
pub struct LlmResponse { pub text: String, pub tokens: TokenUsage }

pub struct LiveClient { /* ureq; OpenAI-compatible chat completions */ }
pub struct RecordedClient { /* replays AgentResponded events by prompt hash */ }
pub struct TemplateClient { /* offline: renders templates/ into a manifest */ }
```

**Agent protocol.** A model response is one JSON object mapping relative paths to file contents. A generated project must return the complete tree; a self-edit returns only changed files because its manifest overlays the recorded base:

```json
{"files": {"src/main.rs": "fn main() {}\n"}}
```

A self-edit with exactly one file target skips JSON: the request switches to `RequestFormat::SingleFile`, whose system prompt demands the file and nothing else, and the model returns that file's complete contents as plain text. A fenced block is unwrapped. The format is part of the prompt hash, and a single-file request omits the JSON `response_format` constraint. A directory target or several targets uses the manifest. The executor validates every path (relative, `/` separators, no `.`/`..`, bounded count and size), replaces `project/` for a generated project, overlays it for a self-edit, and only then runs the gates. Prompt assembly is deterministic: the full spec and the reference template are rendered in declaration/sorted order, so the recorded prompt hash is reproducible.

**Review protocol.** The reviewer answers one JSON object with an approval, concrete issues, and 3–5 short lessons:

```json
{"approve": true, "issues": [], "lessons": ["write tests first", "keep the crate small"]}
```

The executor writes the lessons to `lessons/<task-id>.md`; the raw response remains the event-log record from which that file can be reconstructed.

**LiveClient** speaks the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions wire format. URL, key, per-role model, timeout, and optional token cap come from the environment — `EVENGATE_LLM_URL`, `EVENGATE_LLM_API_KEY`, `EVENGATE_MODEL_PLANNER|EXECUTOR|REVIEWER` (fallback `EVENGATE_MODEL`), `EVENGATE_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECS`, `EVENGATE_LLM_MAX_TOKENS`. Every request sets `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` because both roles must answer with one JSON object; a provider that ignores the field behaves as before. The wire format is fixed; the vendor is not.

**Client selection.** `EVENGATE_LLM=template|live|recorded`. Unset means `live` when `EVENGATE_LLM_URL` is set, otherwise `template`. `TemplateClient` is the deterministic offline agent: it renders `templates/bin` the same way the seed kernel did, so the hello scenario stays reproducible without credentials.

**RecordedClient** reconstructs `AgentInvoked` → `AgentResponded` pairs from the log in order and refuses a request whose role or prompt hash differs. A changed input therefore fails loudly instead of consuming an answer to a different question. Live responses are stored verbatim in `AgentResponded`, so the event log is sufficient to reconstruct what the model returned. `ev replay` itself remains a pure fold and never calls the network.

### 7.6 `gate.rs` — the quality barrier

A gate is a pure function from an artifact set to a verdict:

```rust
pub enum GateResult {
    Pass,
    Fail { reason: String },
    NeedsHuman { question: String },
}

pub trait Gate {
    fn id(&self) -> GateId;
    fn check(&self, ctx: &GateContext) -> GateResult;
}
```

**Mandatory gates for v0:**

| Gate | Kind | Check |
|------|------|-------|
| `Compiles` | Deterministic | `cargo check --locked` in sandbox, exit 0 |
| `TestsPass` | Deterministic | `cargo test --locked`, all green |
| `LintsClean` | Deterministic | `cargo clippy --locked -- -D warnings` |
| `FormatClean` | Deterministic | `cargo fmt --check`, exit 0 |
| `ReviewAgent` | LLM (recorded) | Project tree (path → contents) → structured verdict `{approve: bool, issues: []}` |
| `HumanApproval` | Human | Explicit `HumanApproved` event |

**Rule:** the executing agent has no mechanism to mark a gate as passed. Gates own their verdicts.

For a self-edit the review prompt carries the task spec, the repository path map, and only the files that differ from `SelfEditBase` (plus a deleted-file list); the reviewer judges the change, not a fresh copy of the repository.

`Compiles`, `TestsPass`, `LintsClean`, `FormatClean`, and `ReviewAgent` are the mandatory v0 gates, in that order. `TaskCreated` records that list, so a later gate addition or removal never reinterprets an older task. The review agent runs on the artifact the deterministic gates accepted, records its request and raw response as `Reviewer` events, and maps a withheld approval to `Fail` with the issues as the reason. A rejection stops the run for a human immediately rather than re-asking the same tree; an unusable verdict becomes `NeedsHuman`. Review requires a model: with the offline `TemplateClient` the run stops at this gate with an actionable error and resumes once a model is configured. The executor cannot pass this gate on the reviewer's behalf. From a blocked state the human can `ev revise` (executor re-runs with the verdicts) or `ev abandon`; see §7.3. The verdict's `lessons` are written to `lessons/<task-id>.md` before the gate result is recorded; a revision overwrites the same file.

### 7.7 `sandbox.rs` — process isolation

- Linux: `bwrap` or `firejail` invoked via `std::process::Command`.
- Cross-platform: `docker run --rm --network=none -v <workdir>:/work:ro`.

**Mandatory constraints for every spawned process:**

- Network disabled, except an explicit allowlist to the LLM API endpoint (or no network at all when the LLM runs outside the sandbox).
- Working directory is a **copy** of the task's project directory, mounted **read-only**.
- Read-only container root. The only writable path is a 1 GiB executable `/tmp` tmpfs, which holds `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` and compiler scratch files.
- Memory and swap capped (default 2 GiB each, so the container cannot swap), PID count capped (default 256), CPU capped (default 2).
- All Linux capabilities dropped, `no-new-privileges` set, and an init process reaps orphans.
- Wall-clock timeout (default: 300s).
- Output size cap (default: 1 MiB per stream); excess is truncated with a marker.
- Limits are overridable with `EVENGATE_SANDBOX_MEMORY`, `EVENGATE_SANDBOX_CPUS`, and `EVENGATE_SANDBOX_PIDS`.

The image is built from `sandbox/Dockerfile` with the repository root as the build context. It installs clippy and rustfmt at build time and runs `cargo fetch --locked` on this repository's manifests, so a self-edit gate run can compile Evengate with `--network=none`.

### 7.8 `knowledge.rs` — the accumulator

Knowledge is **structured, versioned, and fed back into prompts**. Not a vector store. Not a RAG index in v0.

**Artifact types:**

| Type | Written by | Consumed by |
|------|------------|-------------|
| `adr/<n>-<slug>.md` | Human or ReviewAgent | All future tasks in the project |
| `lessons/<task-id>.md` | ReviewAgent verdict, written by executor | Prompt assembly for similar tasks |
| `rules/<project>.md` | Human, or promoted from lessons | Every task in the project |
| `codebase-map.md` | Regenerated periodically | Planning agent |
| `patterns/<name>.md` | Promoted from repeated successes | Template selection |

**Feedback mechanism (v0):** the review verdict carries 3–5 `lessons` bullets ("what went wrong, what to do differently"). The executor writes them to `lessons/<task-id>.md`, overwriting on a revision, under the lessons root: `lessons/` in the working directory, overridable with `EVENGATE_LESSONS_DIR`. The next executor prompt includes:

- the current `spec.md` (always),
- `rules/<project>.md`, when present, under the rules root (`rules/` by default, `EVENGATE_RULES_DIR` overrides),
- the 5 most recent `lessons/*.md`, newest first by file modification time, ties broken by file name (recency, not similarity — a similarity index comes later).

The prompt states that the current spec and constraints win over inherited lessons. Rules and lessons are read during prompt assembly, never cached in `State`, so a human edit applies to the next invocation. The same `# Project rules` section is given to the review agent, so a project rule is checked as well as prompted. The review agent also receives the same five most recent lesson files, with an instruction to copy a still-applicable lesson's text exactly instead of rewording it; repetition is therefore observable to the critic, not only to the executor. The raw reviewer response recorded in `AgentResponded` is the event-log source for a lesson file, so `ev replay` remains a pure fold and `ev materialize` can rebuild the file. `codebase-map.md` joins the prompt once a planner consumes it; the lessons path is the v0 feedback loop.

**Promotion path:** after a review writes a lesson file, the executor groups lessons across `lessons/*.md`. Two bullets are the same lesson when their content-token sets reach a Dice coefficient of 3/5 after lowercasing, dropping stopwords and advice framing, and folding simple plurals; a negation on one side and not the other blocks the match. A group counts once per task file, not once per bullet. Its representative is the exact spelling found in the most files, ties broken by canonical key. The executor records a `LessonRepeated { lesson, text, count }` event for every group seen in at least three files that is not already covered by a bullet in `rules/<project>.md`; a promoted paraphrase also suppresses re-proposal. Matching is lexical, so a near-miss is proposed for human review, never auto-promoted.

Once every mandatory gate passes, `machine.rs` pauses before `OpenPullRequest` and emits `Command::RequestHumanReview` with artifact kind `promotion` and the proposal in `detail`. The human decides:

- `ev promote <task-dir> --reviewer <name> [--lesson <text>]` appends the lesson to `rules/<project>.md` and records `LessonPromoted`;
- `ev dismiss <task-dir> --reviewer <name> [--lesson <text>]` records `LessonDismissed` and changes no file.

One lesson is decided per invocation, in canonical key order; the task then asks for the next decision or continues to the PR. Dismissal is recorded in that task's log only: because per-task logs are independent (ADR-0005), the next task proposes the lesson again unless it is promoted. Promotion is always a human decision.

This is Evengate's real moat. A vector index can be added later without changing the artifact schema.

## 8. Specification Format

Task specs are markdown with a fixed heading schema. Parsed by a hand-rolled parser (~30 lines), never by a generic markdown library.

```markdown
# <Task title>

## Goal
One paragraph. What the user wants, in outcome terms.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Concrete, testable criterion
- [ ] ...

## Constraints
- Language, crates allowed, style rules, performance limits.

## Non-goals
- Explicitly out of scope.

## Target
- Repository-relative file or directory this task edits; omit for a generated project.
- A path under `src/` marks the task as a self-edit.

## Context
Links to relevant files, ADRs, prior tasks.

## Open questions
Anything the agent should ask about before starting.
```

If `Goal`, `Acceptance`, or `Constraints` is missing, the spec is rejected at `TaskCreated` and never reaches the LLM. This is cheaper than letting a confused agent burn tokens.
